page.layout: One printed page, left part of a two-column index; the right part is cut off. Running head at top centre, then the alphabetical index in one column with letter headings (H, I, L, M, N) and entries in italic.; One printed page, narrow right-hand strip: a column of page numbers aligned to index entries at left, with the entries themselves mostly cut off; a marginal "X." mark at top left.

l.i: Hyacinthi gemmæ historia. 27. variarum error circa hanc gemmam. ibi
Lipis lapis eiusque vires in medicina.

page.notes: Right part of the page is cut off; the index entries continue beyond the edge. Initial capitals H, I, L, M, N are large decorative letters, read from context. The Greek word in the N entry is transcribed as best read. Marks at the top left of the page (small numerals) are stains or show-through and are not transcribed. Right-hand strip only; the index entries to the left are cut off and mostly unreadable, so only the page numbers and fragments visible are given. Lines are given as their printed numbers. Entries such as "fpecies 28. 29. Neoterico-" and "atura illius. ibid." are partial fragments. The "Nephri-" at the foot is a catchword-like fragment in a different type.
